security_audit.summary: The static backtick detections are Markdown code fences or inline-code examples in SKILL.md, not executable Ruby shell backticks. The hardcoded URLs are GitHub reference links, and the system reconnaissance hit is ordinary best-practice prose. No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or executable payload was found in the single-file skill.

remediation.issue: Visible CLI examples can install or run third-party packages.
remediation.suggestion: State that npm, npx, and MCP registration commands require user review and confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: The memory backup example uses an absolute workspace path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a placeholder path and tell users to choose a project-local backup location.

content.value_statement: Complex projects need coordinated agents, clear topology choices, and visible handoffs. This skill provides reusable Claude Flow swarm patterns for research, development, testing, analysis, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Explains mesh, hierarchical, star, and ring swarm topology selection.
Shows research, development, testing, and analysis swarm architectures.
Defines agent roles, capabilities, and task orchestration examples.
Covers memory namespaces, state snapshots, backups, and recovery patterns.
Includes monitoring, metrics, optimization, and troubleshooting guidance.
limitations: Assumes Claude Flow and MCP tools are available in the user environment.
Provides patterns and examples, not a complete application scaffold.
Command examples require user review before installation or execution.
Does not verify that referenced Claude Flow APIs are current.

use_cases.title: Plan research swarms
use_cases.description: Coordinate researchers, analysts, and writers for structured information gathering and synthesis.

use_cases.title: Organize development delivery
use_cases.description: Map architecture, implementation, testing, review, and deployment work across specialist agents.

use_cases.title: Run distributed quality workflows
use_cases.description: Design testing, security, performance, and reporting swarms for complex validation projects.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a swarm topology
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to design a swarm for [project goal]. Recommend one topology, agent roles, phases, and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a development workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to plan a development swarm for [application]. Include architecture, parallel implementation, testing, review, and deployment coordination.

prompt_templates.title: Design a testing swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to create a testing swarm for [system]. Cover unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and security validation.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and recover a swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to diagnose [swarm problem]. Recommend monitoring checks, memory actions, topology changes, and recovery steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a research swarm for a market analysis project.
output_examples.output: A mesh topology with research, data analysis, pattern analysis, and report writing agents, organized into gather, validate, synthesize, and report phases.

output_examples.input: Coordinate full-stack API delivery with quality gates.
output_examples.output: A hierarchical workflow led by an architect, with parallel backend, frontend, database, testing, review, documentation, and deployment responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Recover a slow swarm that has failing tasks.
output_examples.output: A recovery plan covering status checks, error analysis, bottleneck review, retry strategy, state snapshots, and topology optimization.

best_practices: Choose topology from task dependency, coordination needs, and review depth.
Assign narrow agent roles and define handoff points before parallel work starts.
Monitor status, memory, and resource use during long swarm runs.
anti_patterns: Starting maximum agents before task boundaries are clear.
Mixing dependent and independent tasks in one parallel batch.
Running CLI setup or fallback commands without user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and coordinate Claude Flow swarms for research, development, testing, analysis, and recovery workflows.

faq.question: Does it install Claude Flow?
faq.answer: No. It documents optional setup and fallback commands that users should review before running.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Which topology should I choose?
faq.answer: Use mesh for research, hierarchical for structured delivery, star for centralized testing, and ring for staged pipelines.

faq.question: Does it replace project management?
faq.answer: No. It provides orchestration patterns that still need project goals, review criteria, and human approval.

faq.question: Is it safe for production workflows?
faq.answer: Review commands, package sources, permissions, and data handling before applying any workflow to production systems.
